corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 1920s pole tower; the 1934 Aermotor that replaced it, and stood until 1959, was 80 ft (24.4 m).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts describes an open cab on the 1920s pole tower; Idaho Fire Lookouts and firelookout.com describe a 7x7 cab.

The Binarch sources give an 80-foot tower (1934) that was moved in 1959; the Newport Hill page describes a 40-foot Aermotor tower developed there in 1938. The sources do not say whether the tower was shortened or whether these are different structures.
Idaho Fire Lookouts lists Phil McVay for 1944 to 1946 and also Robert L McVey for the same period.

notes_for_editor: Record height 12.2 m (40 ft) matches the 1920s pole tower; the 1934 Aermotor was 80 ft (24.4 m), proposed as a correction. Design 'Aermotor' is kept, with the two-tower history noted in the summary. The Newport Hill page lists its 40-foot tower as removed, so neither site has a standing tower per these sources. Newport Hill's height (40 ft) conflicts with the 80 ft given for the moved tower. No source describes remains at the original site. Access 'public' is inferred from the hike-in label. Budget: 2 searches and 5 page reads used. The naughtyhiker.com 'footings' passage was checked and is about Cooks Peak, not this site, so it is not used.
